glossary.panelSubtitle: Definitions for the terms that are easiest to misread, and where each number actually comes from.

soc.definition: The percentage of usable energy currently left in the battery, where 100% is a full charge of the pack as it exists today — not as it was when new.
soc.howMeasured: Reported directly by the vehicle. The displayed value already excludes the buffer the car reserves below 0%, so a car at 0% is not an empty pack.

ratedRange.definition: A rating, not a prediction: the current state of charge multiplied by a fixed EPA-derived distance per percent. It ignores weather, speed, terrain and load.
ratedRange.howMeasured: Reported by the vehicle. Because the multiplier is fixed, rated range moves only when state of charge or the pack’s estimated capacity moves — real trips almost always use more.

degradation.howMeasured: Derived from many observed charges over weeks. A single reading is noise: temperature, recent fast charging and a resting pack all shift the estimate by more than a year of real loss.

phantomDrain.howMeasured: Measured only across parked, non-charging windows. Sentry mode, cabin overheat protection, preconditioning and frequent polling all raise it, and each is a setting rather than a fault.

efficiency.howMeasured: Computed from completed drives that report both distance and energy. Charging losses are not included, so a wall-meter figure will always look worse than this one.

signalFreshness.howMeasured: Freshness is the age of the last received value, not a health check. A sleeping vehicle produces stale signals by design; that is normal and costs no range.

stateOfHealth.howMeasured: Estimated from observed full-charge capacity over time. It is an estimate with a real error bar, which is why the trend matters more than any single value.
